title: The Sparrow and the Elephant
text:
A pair of sparrows had built their nest in a tree and laid their eggs. One day a wild elephant, wandering in the heat, broke the branch to shade himself. The nest fell and every egg was smashed. The mother sparrow grieved, and she swore to destroy the elephant.

What could a sparrow do against an elephant? She went to her friend the woodpecker, and together they asked for the help of a gnat and a frog. They made a plan in which each would do only one small thing.

At noon the gnat flew to the elephant's ear and hummed a soft, sweet tune. The elephant closed his eyes with pleasure. At that moment the woodpecker darted in and pecked out his eyes. Blind and in pain, the elephant grew desperately thirsty as the day wore on. Then the frog sat at the edge of a deep pit and croaked. Hearing a frog, the elephant believed there must be water there. He stumbled toward the sound, fell into the pit, and died.
lesson: No single small ally may be able to win, but several with different skills, each doing one part at the right moment, can overcome a much stronger opponent.
people: A sparrow, a woodpecker, a gnat, a frog, an elephant
source: Panchatantra, Book I (The Loss of Friends)
